findings.title: Theft of Unclaimed Yields Due to Improper Reward Distribution in Vault Program
findings.description:
The vault program has a vulnerability in its reward distribution mechanism where the `UpdateVaultBalance` function is not enforced before minting operations or other actions involving `vault.deposited_tokens`. This leads to an incorrect calculation of reward entitlements because the system does not update the vault's token balance before including new depositors in the reward pool.

The root cause is the lack of a mandatory call to `UpdateVaultBalance` prior to minting new tokens. As a result, when rewards are deposited into the vault, they remain unclaimed and are not accounted for until the balance is updated. If a new depositor mints tokens before this update occurs, they are included in the reward distribution calculation despite not contributing to the yield generation.

An attacker can exploit this by monitoring reward deposits and quickly minting tokens before the `UpdateVaultBalance` function is called. This allows them to claim a portion of the unclaimed yield that was generated solely from prior deposits.

The impact is the theft of unclaimed yield from legitimate depositors, leading to direct financial loss. In the provided proof of concept, a depositor who should have received 11,000 tokens only receives 10,500, demonstrating a 500-token loss due to the unfair redistribution.
